candidate.answerReason: The integers run from 2 through 53. Pairing opposite ends gives 26 pairs of sum 55, so the mean is 26·55/52 = 27½.

methods.label: Pair the smallest and largest integers
methods.explanation:
Starting at \(2\), the fifty-second integer is \(2+51=53\). Pair the smallest with the largest, then continue inward:
\[
(2,53),\ (3,52),\ \ldots,\ (27,28).
\]
Each pair sums to \(55\): moving inward increases one entry by \(1\) and decreases the other by \(1\). These \(26\) pairs use all \(52\) integers exactly once. The arithmetic mean is the total divided by the number of integers, so
\[
\text{mean}=\frac{26\cdot55}{52}
=\frac{55}{2}=27\frac12.
\]
The answer is choice C.
methods.levelReason: Equal-sum pairing and the definition of the mean give an elementary arithmetic solution without a sequence formula.

candidate.annotationRationale: Computing the arithmetic mean is the target. Reordering and grouping the integers into equal-sum pairs supplies the total. The written argument derives the needed sum directly, so the arithmetic-sequence summation formula is not a prerequisite.
